categories.name: System Architecture & Runtime
categories.description: High-level structure, components, boundaries, responsibilities, and data flow

The extension's background orchestration layer and state authority.

The expected shape and behavior of data or interactions between components.
The formal definition of a data structure's fields, types, and constraints.
The arrangement and connectivity of components in the system.

Coordinating multiple components or services to achieve a higher-level goal.
Managing the interaction and ordering between multiple concurrent or distributed parts.
A relationship where one component requires another to function.

A component that translates between two incompatible interfaces or platforms.

A lookup structure that maps identifiers to implementations or instances.
A component that directs the behavior of other components in response to input.

The process of defining the architecture, components, interfaces, and data for a system to satisfy requirements.

categories.name: Boundaries & Responsibility
categories.description: Rules, ownership, isolation, and trust constraints between components

terms.definition: A rule that restricts what a component may do, such as preventing the service worker from mutating the page DOM.
The edge between the system being built and all external systems or users.
The dividing line between two components defining what each owns and may access.
A line where privilege, authentication, or security assumptions change.
The explicit limit of what a component is allowed to own or modify.
The declaration of which component is responsible for a piece of state, action, or resource.
The single authoritative location for a given piece of state or configuration.
Hiding internal state and behavior behind a defined interface.
Ensuring a component's failures or state do not unintentionally affect others.
The defined range of authority, visibility, or effect for a component or variable.
The total set of entry points and interfaces exposed by a component.
The scope of damage or disruption if a component fails.
The degree to which components depend on each other's internals.
The degree to which elements within a component belong together and serve a common purpose.
The explicit surface through which two components interact, enforcing what is public and what is internal.
The limit of what a component is allowed to access or perform based on granted permissions.
The limit of what a component is technically able to do within its runtime context.
The part of the system responsible for managing and directing operations.
The part of the system responsible for processing and moving actual data.
A rule that constrains dangerous or unsupported behavior in the system.
A restriction that limits what values, behaviors, or operations are valid.
A condition taken for granted in the design that must hold for the system to work correctly.
A condition that must always be true regardless of system state or execution path.
The separation between different runtime execution contexts such as service worker, content script, and sidepanel.
The point at which ownership or access rights to data change between components.
The point at which authority over execution or decision-making transfers between components.

categories.name: State, Storage & Data Model

The per-tab ownership record that prevents duplicate watch runtimes.

Restoring UI or runtime state from persisted storage.
Restoring state after reload, navigation, or worker restart.

A sanitized export of current settings with sensitive values removed or minimized.
The expected shape of data exchanged between components.
A structured export with defined fields, types, and data shape.
The current condition or value of a component or system at a given moment.
The complete set of data that defines the current state of the application.
State held in memory during execution, reflecting current operation.
State scoped to a single user session or tab.
State accessible by multiple components simultaneously.
State private to a single component or module.
State accessible across the entire application.
Ensuring multiple representations of state agree with each other.
The divergence between two representations of the same state over time.
The process of resolving differences between diverged state representations.
A point-in-time capture of system or component state.
Converting structured data to a storable or transferable format.
Converting stored or transferred data back into its structured form.
Stored data kept for faster future access, avoiding repeated computation or retrieval.
A temporary memory area that holds data before it is processed or written.
A fixed-size circular buffer that overwrites old entries when full.
An ordered collection of items waiting to be processed.
Accumulated work that has not yet been processed.
Keeping data in storage for a defined period before expiration.
The automatic removal or invalidation of data after a time period or condition.
Removing items from a cache or buffer to make space for new entries.
The ability of data to survive beyond the current execution context.
A component that abstracts the details of a specific storage mechanism.
A model that defines valid states and the transitions between them.

categories.name: Events & Messaging
categories.description: How signals, commands, and notifications flow between components

terms.definition: A signal indicating that something happened in the system.
A class of telemetry data such as logs, metrics, or traces.
A condition or event that initiates an action or workflow.
A message informing a component or user that something occurred.
A function passed to another component to be invoked when a condition is met.
A discrete unit of data sent from one component to another.
A shared channel through which components publish and subscribe to events.
A messaging pattern where publishers emit events and subscribers receive those they registered for.
Sending a message or event to its intended recipient or handler.
Producing and sending an event or signal from a component.
Registration to receive events or messages matching specific criteria.
A component or function registered to receive specific events.
A component that watches for state changes or events and reacts accordingly.
An extension point that allows external code to react to lifecycle events.
A mutual acknowledgment exchange establishing communication between two components.
A periodic signal confirming that a runtime or component is still alive.
A response confirming receipt or successful processing of a message.
An ID used to connect related events across components.
An identifier for a specific watch or claim session.

A continuous sequence of events emitted over time.
Re-processing previously captured events to reproduce behavior or recover state.
Preventing the same session from being claimed or processed twice.

Grouping multiple items into fewer writes or operations.
